dedupe_keys.name: ecb investment fund network contagion and climate stress test model working paper 2757

description: This model simulates short-term market risk and the spread of shocks through the investment fund sector, with two contagion channels: funds' cross-holdings of one another and overlapping holdings of the same securities, where sales by some funds lower prices for others. It adds a fund-level view of both transition and physical climate risk exposures and runs stress tests with market and liquidity shocks. It was developed by Régis Gourdel and Matthias Sydow at the European Central Bank and published as Working Paper 2757 in December 2022. It uses complete holdings of open-end and closed-end funds from the Lipper Global Data Feed provided by Refinitiv, well populated from mid-2018 to mid-2020. The paper is free as a PDF; the holdings data are commercial and the pages read do not say whether code is shared. Caveats: the paper reflects the authors' views, not the ECB's, and results depend on the shock design; it finds network amplification of transition shocks less likely, while physical risk is absorbed less well. For simulation it shows how climate shocks to infrastructure and industry assets can cascade through the funds that finance them, a model for stress tests of financial resilience. It is related to the DebtRank NetworkRiskMeasures record in this catalogue, another financial contagion model.
